title: ASan 检测 Native 内存错误：构建、运行与报告解读
key_conclusions: ASan turns memory corruption models into concrete evidence by reporting access stack, allocation stack, free stack, redzones, shadow bytes, and symbolized source lines.
Day 36's OOB, UAF, double free, and invalid free taxonomy maps directly to ASan error types and report fields.
The first engineering step is to verify target shared library, ABI, build variant, runtime loading, and symbol directory before interpreting any report.
Fix acceptance requires replaying the same scenario with no ASan report, no tombstone, and stable related memory evidence.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real Android ASan report captured from a device.
It does not validate concrete Gradle, CMake, or ndk-build ASan flags across NDK and Android Gradle Plugin versions.
It does not include a runnable project that demonstrates heap overflow, UAF, double free, invalid free, stack overflow, and global overflow.
It does not show symbolization failures caused by mismatched build ids or stripped shared libraries.
discovered_connections: Day 36's corruption taxonomy becomes the ASan report reading checklist.
Day 35's tombstone structure remains useful as a fallback when ASan aborts and debuggerd produces a crash artifact.
Day 34's allocator and heapprofd boundaries explain why ASan reports corruption while heapprofd may only show growth.
Day 38 should compare HWASan tag mismatch evidence against ASan redzone and quarantine evidence.
Day 39 should explain when lower-overhead GWP-ASan, Scudo, or MTE is preferable to full ASan builds.
